title: Enterprise questionnaire routing & prioritization framework
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Enterprise customers submit security and compliance requests (SOC2/ISO attestations, HIPAA onboarding, GDPR/DPA clauses, and vendor security questionnaires) through multiple channels (support tickets, sales emails, and direct outreach). This results in inconsistent routing, long SLA times, duplicated effort across Security/Legal/Product, and poor visibility into backlog and prioritization rationale.

Goal: Define a repeatable intake and prioritization framework that triages enterprise security & compliance requirements (including vendor questionnaires) into clear buckets, routes to the appropriate owners, provides SLA expectations to customers, and gives Product + Security a lightweight decision rubric for prioritization and resourcing.
problem_statement: Current intake is fragmented: some questionnaires go straight to Solutions Engineering, others to Legal or Sales; there's no unified scoring for customer risk/impact or engineering effort; customers receive ad-hoc timelines. This slows enterprise deals and increases support burden.
proposed_solution:
1) Single intake surface: create a standardized 'Enterprise Compliance Intake' form surfaced in the Console, Sales intake playbook, and Support macros that captures core fields (customer segment, deal status, questionnaire type, sensitivity, required deadline, legal terms requested, data residency requirements, attachments).

2) Triage engine & scoring rubric: implement a 5-factor scoring model: Data Sensitivity (1-5), Business Impact (1-5), Deal Velocity (1-5), Implementation Effort (1-5), Regulatory Mandate (1-5). Composite score maps to buckets: Tier A (Immediate), Tier B (Sprint), Tier C (Next Quarter), Tier D (Reference/No Action).

3) Routing policy: based on questionnaire type + score, route to owners: Security for SOC2/ISO/GDPR ops items, Legal for contract or DPA edits, Solutions Eng for technical integrations (VPC, audit logs), Product for platform changes (new console features), and Support for clarifications. Include an 'escalate' flag for exec-reviewed requests.

4) SLA & customer communication templates: standardized acknowledgment within 48 hours, preliminary triage summary within 5 business days for Tier A/B, and regular status updates every 7 days. Provide templated responses for common questionnaire items.

5) Platform integration: integrate intake into Linear with auto-created ticket (PM/ENG/SEC labels), add tracking fields (score, bucket, owner, SLA date), and surface a dashboard in Console-Observability (work with ENG-3891).

6) Pilot & rollout: pilot with two enterprise customers and Sales + Support, iterate, then roll out org-wide with training and knowledge base articles.
acceptance_criteria:
- Intake form exists and is accessible from Support macros, Sales playbook, and a Console 'Request Compliance Review' flow.
- A triage rubric document (Confluence) describing scoring and bucket mappings is published and reviewed by Security and Legal.
- Linear automation creates tickets with correct labels and fields; tickets include composite score and assigned owner.
- Routing rules implemented (manual or automation) for at least SOC2, GDPR/DPA, HIPAA, and vendor-questionnaire categories.
- SLA templates and customer-facing acknowledgment messages approved by Comms and Legal.
- Pilot completed with two customers; success metrics collected and review held with stakeholders.
- Security sign-off on any process that touches customer data.
success_metrics:
- Median time-to-first-response for compliance requests reduced from current baseline to <48 hours.
- Percentage of requests with correct owner assignment >= 90% in pilot phase.
- Reduction in duplicate handling (tickets reassigned) by 60%.
- Sales-reported blocker incidents due to compliance questions reduced by 30% within two quarters.
- NPS improvement in enterprise onboarding touchpoint (qualitative feedback).
stakeholders: Product: Marco Rivera; Security: Lina Chen; Legal: Priya Mehta; Solutions Eng: Daniel Gomez; Support: Rosa Alvarez; Sales AE lead: Tom Nguyen; Docs: Maya Singh; Observability/Console Eng: ENG-3891 owner.
rollout_plan:
Phase 0 (Design): Finalize intake schema and scoring rubric; draft communication templates (2 weeks).
Phase 1 (Pilot): Implement form + Linear automation; route pilot requests for two strategic customers (3 weeks).
Phase 2 (Iterate): Incorporate feedback, add routing rules for additional questionnaire types, and add dashboard KPIs (2 weeks).
Phase 3 (Org Rollout): Launch to Sales/Support, publish KB articles, schedule training sessions; monitor SLAs for one quarter.
Phase 4 (Automate): Work with ENG to replace manual routing with automation and integrate visibility into Console-Observability (targeted as follow-on EPIC).
open_questions:
- Which storage location will host attachments for questionnaires (Drive vs. secure S3) and does that change routing? (Legal/Security input required).
- Should the intake include a boolean for 'requires on-prem handling' to gate Private deployment requests?
- What is the long-term home for the triage dashboard (Console vs. internal Confluence dashboard)?
- Can Support trigger a fast-track SLA for pipeline-critical deals and what criteria qualify?
notes:
- Align with PM-5910 on DPA templates to avoid duplicated work.
- Include a mini-FAQ for common SOC2 control evidence items to reduce back-and-forth.
- Legal prefers initial 'information only' routing for DPAs before substantive negotiation.
- Security requests that any form capturing PHI be flagged for HIPAA review immediately.
- Consider tagging questionnaires with a canonical taxonomy (SOC2, ISO27001, HIPAA, GDPR/DPA, Vendor-Security-Questionnaire) to aid analytics.
decisions:
- Use a composite numeric scoring model rather than categorical-only to enable tie-breaking and aggregation.
- Pilot will only include manual routing rules; automation is scoped as a follow-on.
- Acknowledgment SLA set to 48 hours for all intake submissions (agreed by Support & Comms).
